html:
The Bou Inania Madrasa is a college for students of religion in Fez, built from 1350 to 1355 by the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris. It is the masterpiece of Marinid art.

The Marinids, a Berber dynasty that ruled Morocco from the 1200s to the 1400s, built many madrasas around the Qarawiyyin to train scholars and judges loyal to them. Bou Inania is the grandest. Its courtyard is covered in carved cedar, stucco and tiles, and it had a water clock on the street outside.

It is one of the few working religious buildings in Morocco that non-Muslims may enter. With the rest of old Fez it is a World Heritage Site.
